artifact: S-376 / CR-120 post-change coverage baseline for the reference workspace
measured_by: logos-core/tests/coverage_headline_baseline.rs, through the same discover -> EngineRegistry(Lazy) -> cross_service_coverage construction `logos workspace status` uses
reconciled_against: logos-docs/ws-status-2026-09-08-v1.4.7.json — the pre-change capture sprint 66 §7 names for this purpose — for the CONTRACT-SURFACE half only, which reproduces from it cell for cell (81 bound / 146 ambiguous / 1 unbound / 646 no-provider). The invocation half no longer reproduces and must not be expected to: this store was re-indexed on 2026-09-13 with the S-397 T1 accessor hop, which is the whole subject of the S-374 and S-397 deltas below.
read_only_proof: This HARNESS is read-only — it opens each member's existing store and reads it. The store it read was re-indexed once, deliberately and by hand, immediately before the run (see generation.index_built_on): 84 members, `logos --project <member> index`, exit 0 on every one, 7,895 files and 93,249 nodes in 67 s. That re-index is the S-397 T2 measurement step recorded in logos-core/tests/config_bound_admission/config_bound_admission_finding.txt; it is stated here rather than implied, because a figure whose index generation is unattributable is the defect this artifact exists to prevent.

generation.index_built_by: logos 1.4.9 + S-397 T1 (worktree sprint-68-I2-S1, merge base dbc1c443)
generation.why: Refusal rows and configuration-bound targets are both written at INDEX time. This store was re-indexed on 2026-09-13 from a binary carrying S-374 and S-397 T1, so it holds both: 87 `base-url-runtime` refusal rows and 44 rows whose target is a resolved configuration placeholder. The previous generation of this artifact was a post-CR-120 PAYLOAD SHAPE over a pre-S-374 INDEX GENERATION (1.4.7, 2026-09-08); that caveat is now discharged, and the contract-surface half is unchanged across the two generations, which is what makes the comparison sound.
generation.refresh_procedure: At the sprint-review human gate, on a binary built from this sprint's merged main: (1) `logos init --workspace --yes` at ~/source/pec-services — this re-enrols the root and spawns the detached warm supervisor that indexes the 84 members (~43 s to return; a root `logos index` covers the ROOT ONLY, 3 files, and that is correct). (2) Wait for `.logos.workspace.warm.json` to report every member warm. (3) Re-run this harness with `LOGOS_REF_WORKSPACE=~/source/pec-services LOGOS_BASELINE_WRITE=1 cargo test -p logos-core --test coverage_headline_baseline -- --nocapture`, which rewrites the `measurement` block below. (4) Restate the `deltas` entries whose status is `pending-reindex` as `observed`, with the figures the run produced. (5) Commit the artifact and the finding beside it.
generation.figures_the_refresh_would_change: DISCHARGED — the refresh has been run and every figure below is observed rather than predicted. The prediction is kept here because it verified: S-374's recorded workspace-wide count is 131 client-call rows, and the re-index wrote exactly 131 route/invocation rows (132 ledger `http-client-call` rows less the one TypeScript e2e site that was already present). They did not all land as refusals, because S-397 T1's accessor hop resolved 44 of them: 131 = 87 `base-url-runtime` refusals + 44 `config-bound` rows. `resolved_cross_service_edges` stayed 0 exactly as predicted — a `config-bound` row is excluded from it by construction — while `egress_resolution` moved off 0.000 for the first time, to 0.032 (5 of 155), because 5 of the 44 admitted rows bind a provider.

headline_reading: ZERO cross-service edges in this estate are resolved from a captured call site, over 155 captured egress sites — while the retired bound_ratio reads 0.225 on the same data and the pooled `bound` reads 86. 81 of those 86 are contract-surface matches (an OpenAPI operation matched to a controller route); by_intake.invocation.bound is 5, up from 0, and all 5 are configuration-bound client calls that bind a provider without drawing an edge. That contrast is CR-120's entire case, and the move from 0 to 5 is S-397's.

S-374.story: The HTTP client-call arm records its refusals
S-374.effect: NOW OBSERVED. The 2026-09-13 re-index wrote 131 route/invocation rows where the 1.4.7 store held 1 — the workspace-wide figure S-374 recorded, landing at the upper end of the predicted 115-131 range exactly as the prediction said an index run would. 87 of them are `base-url-runtime` refusals and the other 44 are S-397 T1's configuration-bound rows, so the `unbound` column rose by 87 rather than by 131: the prediction's magnitude is confirmed and its split was not foreseen, because S-397 T1 had not been written when it was made. `egress_resolution_measured` 54 -> 155 and `spec_conformance_measured` 282 -> 383; `spec_conformance_ratio` 0.287 -> 0.225. `resolved_cross_service_edges` stayed 0 as predicted.

S-375.story: The client-call detector gate is receiver-grained, not file-grained
S-375.effect: ZERO change to every figure here, and that zero is a measured result rather than an absence. The narrowing removed 4 Java sites, all verified false positives (three list-index accesses and a cookie-map put), none of which emitted a reference: the workspace-wide genuine `http-client-call` reference count is 1 before and 1 after. Its real effect is on S-374's denominator on the NEXT index: against a file-grained gate, refusal recording would have written 4 ledger rows for a list index and a cookie put, so the range above would have been 4 rows wider at each end — the 'manufactures a coverage denominator out of ordinary code' hazard CR-120 §7 names, avoided.
S-375.evidence: sprint-impl-66.md, S-375 reference-workspace measurement table (before/after 98 -> 94 Java sites, 1 -> 1 workspace emitted)

S-377.story: Coverage reports its intake on every row
S-377.effect: Additive to the payload, and it moves NO count: `intake` became unconditional on all 929 rows (848 of which carried none) and the `by_intake` block was added, derived from the same tally the four headline counters are now derived from. It is what makes this baseline's decisive figure legible at all — `by_intake.invocation.bound: 0` beside a headline `bound: 81`. Measured payload cost on the reference workspace's shape: +2.9% compact bytes.

S-376.story: Retire the bound-ratio; the headline is a resolved-edge count (this story)
S-376.effect: Renames three summary fields and adds four; moves no classification count. `bound_ratio 0.287` is now `spec_conformance_ratio 0.287` with its composed line byte-identical, and the new headline reads `resolved_cross_service_edges: 0` with `egress_resolution: 0.000 (0 of 54 egress sites resolved)`. Measured payload cost on the reference workspace's shape: under 0.1% compact bytes, all of it on the summary object and none per-row.

S-397.story: The accessor capture hop reaches the invocation arm
S-397.effect: The whole of the invocation column's bound and ambiguous halves: 0 -> 5 bound and 0 -> 9 ambiguous, plus 30 `no-provider-in-workspace`, being the 44 rows that now carry `config-bound` provenance where the 1.4.7 store carried none. It is also why the `unbound` rise is 87 and not 131 (see S-374). Measured against S-397 AC2's floor of 79 the 44 is a SHORTFALL, diagnosed in the evidence below as the qualified-receiver ceiling; this artifact records the payload effect, not the verdict.

measurement.resolved_edges_summary: 0 resolved cross-service edges; egress resolution 0.032 (5 of 155 egress sites resolved)
